text:
git reset -q && git add src/ir_lower/stmt/static_property_writes.rs src/types/checker/stmt_check/assignments/properties.rs src/types/checker/stmt_check/assignments/static_properties.rs tests/codegen/types.rs tests/codegen/types/static_property_hash.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(types): a string key into a `static array` property was refused, then lost

`public static array $store = []` refused `self::$store[$k] = $v` outright — `Array index
must be integer` — while the INSTANCE property one line away accepted the same write and
promoted the property to hash storage. php runs both. The shape came out of php's own
userspace stream-wrapper idiom, where the wrapper keeps its bodies in a static map keyed by
URL, so this rejected an entire way of writing a documented feature.

Accepting it in the checker alone would have been a false win, and briefly was: the
lowering's static write path had no associative branch either, so the write fell through to
the Mixed fallback while every READ of the same property loaded it as a hash. Two writes
then `count(self::$store)` answered 0, in silence — the checker and the backend each
believing something the other did not.

Both halves now come from the instance path rather than from a second implementation. The
checker shares `updated_array_property_assign_type` (its label is a parameter now) and the
guard that decides when a DECLARED `array` may record hash storage, so a declared
`array<int>` is still not widened by a string key. The lowering gets the assoc branch the
instance write has always had.

`[$a, $b] = stream_socket_pair(...)` came along: `TypeSpec` has no array form, so every
builtin answering an array declares `mixed`, and list unpacking refused a `mixed`
right-hand side. What the value turns out to be is php's question to answer at run time,
exactly as it is for `[$a] = $untypedParameter`.
